title: Grade 4 ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — 3.2 Belief in Angels

pages.lesson:
PAGE 1: Overview

OVERVIEW
========

Belief in the angels is a pillar of Iman. Angels are honoured creatures of Allah who never disobey Him. In this sub-strand you will name Jibril, Mikail, Raqib and Atid, Malakul Maut (Izrail) and Israfil, and you will learn the duty of each.

## Strand 3.0: Pillars of Iman
Sub-strand 3.2: Belief in Angels
Suggested lessons: 4

## What this sub-strand covers
• Jibril
• Mikail
• Raqib and Atid
• Malakul Maut (Izrail)
• Israfil

## Source
• KICD Grade 4 Islamic Religious Education Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Strand 3.0 Pillars of Iman, Sub-strand 3.2 Belief in Angels
• Qur’an 2:98, 32:11, 39:68, 50:17-18, 66:6 and 82:10-12
• Sahih Muslim: the angels were created from light

## Learning outcomes
By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to:
a) mention the names of the selected angels to strengthen their faith
b) explain the duties of the selected angels as a pillar of Iman
c) appreciate angels as Allah’s creation as a Pillar of Iman

## Key inquiry questions
1. What are the duties of angels?
2. Why did Allah (S.W.T.) create angels?

PAGE 2: How we will learn

## Learning experiences
• name the angels of Allah, (Jibril, Mikail,Raqib and Atid, Izrail and Israfil)
• match and sort the names of angels and their corresponding duties using flash cards/pocket boards
• find names of angels from a crossword puzzle, in pairs or small groups
• search and sing qasida on angels and their duties from a digital device
• brainstorm on the duties of angels in their lives, in pairs or small groups, and write the points in their notebook

## Core competencies
• Communication and collaboration: the skills of speaking and writing are enhanced as learners discuss the significance of angels in their lives, in pairs or small groups, and write their points in their notebooks.
• Critical thinking and problem solving: the skill of interpretation and inference is enhanced as learners find names of angels from a crossword puzzle, in pairs or small groups.
• Self–efficacy: the skill of effective communication is enhanced as learners sing qasida on angels and their duties from a digital device.

## Values
• Responsibility: self-drive as learners search and sing qasida on angels and their duties from a digital device.
• Respect: open-mindedness as learners respect each other’s opinions as they discuss the significance of angels in their lives.

## Pertinent and contemporary issues
• Self-awareness as learners will be cautious in carrying out his duties.

## Links to other learning areas
• English: reading skills as learners acquire new vocabularies while discussing the names of angels and their duties.

PAGE 3: Lesson 1: Angels and the pillar of Iman

LESSON 1: ANGELS AND THE PILLAR OF IMAN
=======================================

## What you will learn
• Name the selected angels.
• State that belief in angels is a pillar of Iman.
• Describe what Muslims believe about angels as Allah’s creation.

Curriculum outcomes: a) mention the names of the selected angels to strengthen their faith; c) appreciate angels as Allah’s creation as a Pillar of Iman

## Introduction
You cannot see them arranging the rows of a lesson, yet a Muslim believes they are real. The angels are a creation of Allah, and believing in them is one of the pillars of Iman.

## Notes

### A pillar of faith
Iman includes belief in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and the decree of good and evil. Belief in the angels is the second of these pillars. A person who denies the angels has left this pillar out of faith.

PAGE 4: Lesson 1: Angels and the pillar of Iman — What angels are

### What angels are
Angels are created by Allah. A Hadith in Sahih Muslim says that the angels were created from light. They do not eat, drink or sleep as people do. They do not disobey Allah, and they do what He commands (Qur’an 66:6). They worship Him constantly. They are not the sons or daughters of Allah, and it is forbidden to worship them. We respect them because Allah created them and gave them duties.

We do not usually see them in their true form. Jibril (alayhis-salam) sometimes came to the Prophet (S.A.W.) in the form of a man. Their real nature is known through revelation, not through guessing.

PAGE 5: Lesson 1: Angels and the pillar of Iman — The angels you will name

### The angels you will name
In this sub-strand the selected angels are:

- Jibril
- Mikail
- Raqib and Atid
- Malakul Maut (Izrail)
- Israfil

Learn to pronounce each name. Later lessons will join each name to a duty. For now, be able to list them and to say why a Muslim believes in them: Allah has told us about them, and belief in them is part of Iman. Appreciating them begins by accepting that they are real, honoured, and busy with Allah’s command.

## Key words
• angel (malak) — a creature of light who obeys Allah and carries out His commands
• Iman — faith
• pillar of Iman — one of the main beliefs that faith stands on

PAGE 6: Lesson 1: Angels and the pillar of Iman — Example 1

## Worked examples

### Example 1
A classmate says, “I will believe in angels only when I see one.” What should a Muslim answer?

Working:
1. Belief in the unseen, including angels, is part of Iman.
2. Allah has informed us of them in the Qur’an and through the Prophet (S.A.W.).
3. Not seeing them does not mean they are absent.

Answer: A Muslim believes in the angels because Allah has told us about them, even though we do not see them in their true form.

## Activity: Name the selected angels
You will need: Name cards, Notebook

1. Listen to the teacher say: Jibril, Mikail, Raqib, Atid, Izrail (Malakul Maut) and Israfil.

2. Repeat the names until the group can say them in order.

3. Write the names in your notebook under the heading “Angels I believe in”.

4. Tell a partner why belief in angels is a pillar of Iman.

PAGE 7: Lesson 2: Jibril and Mikail

## Practice

1. Name the selected angels in this sub-strand.

2. From what were the angels created, according to the Hadith in Sahih Muslim?

3. Do angels disobey Allah?

## Answers to practice

1. Jibril, Mikail, Raqib and Atid, Malakul Maut (Izrail) and Israfil.

2. From light.

3. No. They do what Allah commands.

## Summary
• Belief in the angels is a pillar of Iman.
• Angels are created from light, and they do not disobey Allah.
• The selected angels are Jibril, Mikail, Raqib, Atid, Izrail and Israfil.

LESSON 2: JIBRIL AND MIKAIL
===========================

## What you will learn
• Explain the duty of Jibril.
• Explain the duty of Mikail.
• Show why these duties matter in a Muslim’s life.

Curriculum outcomes: a) mention the names of the selected angels to strengthen their faith; b) explain the duties of the selected angels as a pillar of Iman

## Introduction
The Qur’an you recite reached the Prophet (S.A.W.) through an angel. The rain that grows maize is also under an angel’s duty, by Allah’s command. Those two angels are Jibril and Mikail.

PAGE 8: Lesson 2: Jibril and Mikail — Jibril (alayhis-salam)

## Notes

### Jibril (alayhis-salam)
Jibril is the angel of revelation. He brought Allah’s words to the prophets. He brought the Qur’an to Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.). The first revelation came to the Prophet while he was in the cave of Hira, when Jibril came to him. Jibril is also called Ruh al-Qudus, the Holy Spirit, in the Qur’an, in the sense of this pure angel, not in any other meaning. Muslims send peace on him when they mention him: alayhis-salam.

Because of Jibril’s duty, we have the Qur’an to recite in swalah. Every time you read Al-Fatiha, you are using a message that Allah sent by this angel. Love of the Qur’an is a way of appreciating that duty.

PAGE 9: Lesson 2: Jibril and Mikail — What this means for you

### Mikail (alayhis-salam)
Mikail is entrusted with rain and with provision, rizq, by Allah’s command. Crops, rivers and the food on a plate are not accidents. Allah provides, and He has given Mikail this duty. The Qur’an mentions Mikail among those whom a believer must not take as an enemy (Qur’an 2:98).

### What this means for you
When rain falls, thank Allah, and remember that His angel carries out the command. When you recite Qur’an, thank Allah for sending Jibril to the Prophet (S.A.W.). Do not worship either angel. Thankfulness belongs to Allah, who created them and who sends both revelation and rain.

## Key words
• Jibril — the angel who brought revelation to the prophets
• Mikail — the angel entrusted with rain and provision
• rizq — provision from Allah

PAGE 10: Lesson 2: Jibril and Mikail — Example 1

## Worked examples

### Example 1
During a drought a learner says, “Rain has nothing to do with faith.” How do you answer using the duty of Mikail, without forgetting Allah?

Working:
1. Allah is the Provider.
2. Mikail is entrusted with rain and provision by Allah’s command.
3. The learner should make dua to Allah for rain and thank Him when it comes.

Answer: Allah sends provision, and Mikail carries out the duty of rain by His command. We ask Allah, not the angel.

## Activity: Match Jibril and Mikail with their duties
You will need: Flash cards of names and duties, Notebook

1. Place the name cards Jibril and Mikail on the desk.

2. Match them with the duty cards: revelation, and rain and provision.

3. In pairs, explain why each duty matters to a Grade 4 learner.

4. Write two sentences in your notebook, one for each angel.

PAGE 11: Lesson 3: Raqib, Atid, Izrail and Israfil

## Practice

1. What is the duty of Jibril?

2. What is the duty of Mikail?

3. Should a Muslim worship Jibril because he brought the Qur’an?

## Answers to practice

1. He brings Allah’s revelation to the prophets. He brought the Qur’an to Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.).

2. He is entrusted with rain and provision by Allah’s command.

3. No. Worship is for Allah alone. Jibril obeys Allah.

## Summary
• Jibril brought revelation, including the Qur’an, to the Prophet (S.A.W.).
• Mikail is entrusted with rain and provision.
• We thank Allah for both duties and we do not worship the angels.

LESSON 3: RAQIB, ATID, IZRAIL AND ISRAFIL
=========================================

## What you will learn
• Explain the duties of Raqib and Atid.
• Explain the duties of Malakul Maut and Israfil.
• Match each selected angel with the correct duty.

Curriculum outcomes: a) mention the names of the selected angels to strengthen their faith; b) explain the duties of the selected angels as a pillar of Iman

## Introduction
Two angels write what you say and do. Another will take the soul when the appointed time comes. Another will blow the trumpet that begins the Day of Judgement. Their names are part of a Muslim’s faith.

PAGE 12: Lesson 3: Raqib, Atid, Izrail and Israfil — Raqib and Atid

## Notes

### Raqib and Atid
Raqib and Atid are the recording angels who stay with every person. The Qur’an speaks of two receivers, one on the right and one on the left, and says that a person does not utter a word without an observer ready (Qur’an 50:17-18). It also speaks of noble scribes who record what people do (Qur’an 82:10-12). One records good deeds and the other records bad deeds. Nothing of that record is lost.

### Malakul Maut (Izrail)
Malakul Maut means the Angel of Death. The Qur’an says the angel of death will take the souls (Qur’an 32:11). He is also called Izrail in Islamic teaching. He takes a soul only when Allah has appointed that time. He does not act by his own wish. Remembering him should push a learner to obey Allah, not to tell frightening stories or to be cruel.

PAGE 13: Lesson 3: Raqib, Atid, Izrail and Israfil — Israfil

### Israfil
Israfil will blow the trumpet. The Qur’an describes a blast after which those in the heavens and the earth fall unconscious, except whom Allah wills, and a later blast after which they stand, looking (Qur’an 39:68). The first blast brings the end of this world as we know it, and the next blast is the resurrection for judgement.

Learn the four duties until you can match them without the chart: recorders, Angel of Death, and the angel of the trumpet. These duties are signs that this life is written, that it will end, and that it will be judged.

PAGE 14: Lesson 3: Raqib, Atid, Izrail and Israfil — Example 1

## Key words
• Raqib and Atid — the two angels who record a person’s deeds
• Malakul Maut (Izrail) — the Angel of Death, who takes souls by Allah’s command
• Israfil — the angel who will blow the trumpet

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Sort these duties under the right names: blowing the trumpet, taking the soul, writing good and bad deeds.

Working:
1. Israfil blows the trumpet.
2. Malakul Maut (Izrail) takes the soul at the appointed time.
3. Raqib and Atid record the deeds.

Answer: Israfil: the trumpet. Izrail: the soul. Raqib and Atid: the record of deeds.

PAGE 15: Lesson 3: Raqib, Atid, Izrail and Israfil — Angel crossword and matching cards

## Activity: Angel crossword and matching cards
You will need: A simple crossword or word search with the six names, Duty flash cards, Notebook

1. In pairs, find the names Jibril, Mikail, Raqib, Atid, Izrail and Israfil in the puzzle.

2. Match each name card with its duty card on the pocket board or desk.

3. Check another pair and correct any mismatch.

4. Write the full list of names and duties in your notebook.

## Practice

1. What do Raqib and Atid do?

2. Who is Malakul Maut, and what is his duty?

3. What will Israfil do?

4. Which Qur’an reference speaks of the two receivers who record words?

## Answers to practice

1. They record a person’s deeds. One records good deeds and the other records bad deeds.

2. He is the Angel of Death, also called Izrail. He takes souls when Allah has appointed the time.

3. He will blow the trumpet for the events of the Last Day, as the Qur’an describes.

4. Qur’an 50:17-18.

## Summary
• Raqib and Atid record good and bad deeds.
• Izrail, the Angel of Death, takes souls by Allah’s command.
• Israfil will blow the trumpet.

PAGE 16: Lesson 4: Living with belief in the angels

LESSON 4: LIVING WITH BELIEF IN THE ANGELS
==========================================

## What you will learn
• Explain how the duties of the angels affect daily choices.
• Show appreciation for the angels as Allah’s creation.
• Use a class qasida to remember names and duties.

Curriculum outcomes: b) explain the duties of the selected angels as a pillar of Iman; c) appreciate angels as Allah’s creation as a Pillar of Iman

## Introduction
Belief in the recording angels should make a person careful, not hopeless. A good word is written, and a bad word is written. This lesson turns that knowledge into careful speech and hopeful deeds.

## Notes

### Why Allah created the angels
Allah created the angels to worship Him and to carry out His commands. Their duties serve His wisdom: revelation is delivered, provision is managed by His leave, deeds are recorded, souls are taken at the right time, and the trumpet will be blown when He wills. They are a sign of His power and of His care for the universe.

PAGE 17: Lesson 4: Living with belief in the angels — What their duties mean for a learner

### What their duties mean for a learner
- Because Jibril brought the Qur’an, we recite it respectfully and follow it.
- Because Mikail’s duty concerns rain and rizq, we thank Allah for food and we do not waste it.
- Because Raqib and Atid write our deeds, we choose words and actions we would be happy to see in the record. A kind word is worth saying. A lie is not worth the line it will fill.
- Because Izrail will take the soul at an appointed time, we do not delay a good deed as if we owned tomorrow.
- Because Israfil will blow the trumpet, we believe the Day of Judgement is real and we prepare for it.

PAGE 18: Lesson 4: Living with belief in the angels — Example 1

### Appreciation
We appreciate the angels by believing in them, speaking of them with respect, and refusing jokes that insult them. We do not draw them as we imagine, and we do not worship them. A class qasida can help memory: “Jibril brought the Book we read, Mikail brings the rain we need, Raqib and Atid write the deed, Izrail calls the soul, Israfil’s trumpet wakes the world, by Allah’s leave alone.” Use the song to remember, and use your behaviour to show that the belief is alive.

## Key words
• record of deeds — the writing of good and bad actions kept by the recording angels
• appreciate — to value the angels by believing in them and respecting them

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Two learners start to mock a classmate with a rude nickname. One of them remembers Raqib and Atid. What changes?

Working:
1. The words would be recorded.
2. He stops the nickname and says a kind word instead.
3. The kind word is also recorded.

Answer: He stops the insult because it would be written, and he chooses a good word that will be written instead.

PAGE 19: Lesson 4: Living with belief in the angels — Qasida and a notebook of duties

## Activity: Qasida and a notebook of duties
You will need: Digital device to find a suitable qasida with the teacher, or the class lines above, Notebook

1. With the teacher, listen to or sing a qasida on the angels and their duties. If no suitable recording is available, learn the class lines.

2. In pairs, brainstorm how each duty touches your life and write five points.

3. Share one point with the class and listen respectfully to other opinions.

4. Copy the corrected points into your notebook.

PAGE 20: Lesson 4: Living with belief in the angels — Answers to practice

## Practice

1. Why did Allah create the angels?

2. How should belief in Raqib and Atid change a learner’s speech?

3. Give two ways of appreciating the angels without worshipping them.

## Answers to practice

1. To worship Him and to carry out His commands.

2. The learner avoids lies and insults because they are recorded, and chooses good words that are also recorded.

3. Believe in them, speak of them with respect, follow the Qur’an Jibril brought, and thank Allah for the duties they carry out.

## Summary
• Angels worship Allah and carry out His commands.
• Their duties encourage careful speech, thankfulness, and preparation for the Last Day.
• We respect angels and we worship Allah alone.

PAGE 21: Revision quiz

REVISION QUIZ
=============

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. Belief in the angels is…
   A. a story we may ignore
   B. a pillar of Iman
   C. a type of najasa
   D. only for adults

2. The angels were created from…
   A. clay
   B. light
   C. fire like the jinn only
   D. water

3. Who brought the Qur’an to Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.)?
   A. Mikail
   B. Israfil
   C. Jibril
   D. Raqib

4. Mikail is entrusted with…
   A. recording nicknames only
   B. rain and provision
   C. the trumpet only
   D. building the Ka’bah

5. Raqib and Atid are…
   A. the recording angels
   B. two prophets
   C. two surahs
   D. types of wudhu

6. Malakul Maut (Izrail) takes the soul…

7. Who will blow the trumpet?
   A. Jibril
   B. Mikail
   C. Israfil
   D. Atid

8. Which verse group speaks of two angels receiving a person’s words?
   A. Qur’an 50:17-18
   B. Qur’an 1:1 only
   C. A class song only
   D. Qur’an 112 only

9. A learner stops an insult because it will be written. This shows belief in which angels?
   A. Raqib and Atid
   B. only the rules of football
   C. Al-Masad as an angel
   D. horse riding

10. What is the correct way to appreciate the angels?
   A. worship them
   B. believe in them, respect them, and worship Allah alone
   C. deny them until we see them
   D. draw them as we imagine

PAGE 22: Quiz answers

ANSWERS
=======

1. B. a pillar of Iman
   It is one of the pillars of faith.

2. B. light
   Sahih Muslim reports that the angels were created from light.

3. C. Jibril
   Jibril is the angel of revelation.

4. B. rain and provision
   His duty concerns rain and rizq, by Allah’s command.

5. A. the recording angels
   They record good and bad deeds.

6. When Allah has appointed that person’s time.
   He acts by Allah’s command, as the Angel of Death.

7. C. Israfil
   Israfil will blow the trumpet for the events described in the Qur’an.

8. A. Qur’an 50:17-18
   Surat Qaf describes the two receivers, on the right and on the left.

9. A. Raqib and Atid
   The recording angels write what people say and do.

10. B. believe in them, respect them, and worship Allah alone
   They are honoured creation. Worship belongs to Allah alone.

studyPages.title: Lesson 1: Angels and the pillar of Iman
studyPages.body:
LESSON 1: ANGELS AND THE PILLAR OF IMAN
=======================================

## What you will learn
• Name the selected angels.
• State that belief in angels is a pillar of Iman.
• Describe what Muslims believe about angels as Allah’s creation.

Curriculum outcomes: a) mention the names of the selected angels to strengthen their faith; c) appreciate angels as Allah’s creation as a Pillar of Iman

## Introduction
You cannot see them arranging the rows of a lesson, yet a Muslim believes they are real. The angels are a creation of Allah, and believing in them is one of the pillars of Iman.

## Notes

### A pillar of faith
Iman includes belief in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and the decree of good and evil. Belief in the angels is the second of these pillars. A person who denies the angels has left this pillar out of faith.

studyPages.title: Lesson 1: Angels and the pillar of Iman — What angels are
studyPages.body:
### What angels are
Angels are created by Allah. A Hadith in Sahih Muslim says that the angels were created from light. They do not eat, drink or sleep as people do. They do not disobey Allah, and they do what He commands (Qur’an 66:6). They worship Him constantly. They are not the sons or daughters of Allah, and it is forbidden to worship them. We respect them because Allah created them and gave them duties.

We do not usually see them in their true form. Jibril (alayhis-salam) sometimes came to the Prophet (S.A.W.) in the form of a man. Their real nature is known through revelation, not through guessing.

studyPages.title: Lesson 1: Angels and the pillar of Iman — The angels you will name
studyPages.body:
### The angels you will name
In this sub-strand the selected angels are:

- Jibril
- Mikail
- Raqib and Atid
- Malakul Maut (Izrail)
- Israfil

Learn to pronounce each name. Later lessons will join each name to a duty. For now, be able to list them and to say why a Muslim believes in them: Allah has told us about them, and belief in them is part of Iman. Appreciating them begins by accepting that they are real, honoured, and busy with Allah’s command.

## Key words
• angel (malak) — a creature of light who obeys Allah and carries out His commands
• Iman — faith
• pillar of Iman — one of the main beliefs that faith stands on

studyPages.title: Lesson 1: Angels and the pillar of Iman — Example 1
studyPages.body:
## Worked examples

### Example 1
A classmate says, “I will believe in angels only when I see one.” What should a Muslim answer?

Working:
1. Belief in the unseen, including angels, is part of Iman.
2. Allah has informed us of them in the Qur’an and through the Prophet (S.A.W.).
3. Not seeing them does not mean they are absent.

Answer: A Muslim believes in the angels because Allah has told us about them, even though we do not see them in their true form.

## Activity: Name the selected angels
You will need: Name cards, Notebook

1. Listen to the teacher say: Jibril, Mikail, Raqib, Atid, Izrail (Malakul Maut) and Israfil.

2. Repeat the names until the group can say them in order.

3. Write the names in your notebook under the heading “Angels I believe in”.

4. Tell a partner why belief in angels is a pillar of Iman.

studyPages.title: Lesson 2: Jibril and Mikail
studyPages.body:
## Practice

1. Name the selected angels in this sub-strand.

2. From what were the angels created, according to the Hadith in Sahih Muslim?

3. Do angels disobey Allah?

## Answers to practice

1. Jibril, Mikail, Raqib and Atid, Malakul Maut (Izrail) and Israfil.

2. From light.

3. No. They do what Allah commands.

## Summary
• Belief in the angels is a pillar of Iman.
• Angels are created from light, and they do not disobey Allah.
• The selected angels are Jibril, Mikail, Raqib, Atid, Izrail and Israfil.

LESSON 2: JIBRIL AND MIKAIL
===========================

## What you will learn
• Explain the duty of Jibril.
• Explain the duty of Mikail.
• Show why these duties matter in a Muslim’s life.

Curriculum outcomes: a) mention the names of the selected angels to strengthen their faith; b) explain the duties of the selected angels as a pillar of Iman

## Introduction
The Qur’an you recite reached the Prophet (S.A.W.) through an angel. The rain that grows maize is also under an angel’s duty, by Allah’s command. Those two angels are Jibril and Mikail.

studyPages.title: Lesson 2: Jibril and Mikail — Jibril (alayhis-salam)
studyPages.body:
## Notes

### Jibril (alayhis-salam)
Jibril is the angel of revelation. He brought Allah’s words to the prophets. He brought the Qur’an to Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.). The first revelation came to the Prophet while he was in the cave of Hira, when Jibril came to him. Jibril is also called Ruh al-Qudus, the Holy Spirit, in the Qur’an, in the sense of this pure angel, not in any other meaning. Muslims send peace on him when they mention him: alayhis-salam.

Because of Jibril’s duty, we have the Qur’an to recite in swalah. Every time you read Al-Fatiha, you are using a message that Allah sent by this angel. Love of the Qur’an is a way of appreciating that duty.

studyPages.title: Lesson 2: Jibril and Mikail — What this means for you
studyPages.body:
### Mikail (alayhis-salam)
Mikail is entrusted with rain and with provision, rizq, by Allah’s command. Crops, rivers and the food on a plate are not accidents. Allah provides, and He has given Mikail this duty. The Qur’an mentions Mikail among those whom a believer must not take as an enemy (Qur’an 2:98).

### What this means for you
When rain falls, thank Allah, and remember that His angel carries out the command. When you recite Qur’an, thank Allah for sending Jibril to the Prophet (S.A.W.). Do not worship either angel. Thankfulness belongs to Allah, who created them and who sends both revelation and rain.

## Key words
• Jibril — the angel who brought revelation to the prophets
• Mikail — the angel entrusted with rain and provision
• rizq — provision from Allah

studyPages.title: Lesson 2: Jibril and Mikail — Example 1
studyPages.body:
## Worked examples

### Example 1
During a drought a learner says, “Rain has nothing to do with faith.” How do you answer using the duty of Mikail, without forgetting Allah?

Working:
1. Allah is the Provider.
2. Mikail is entrusted with rain and provision by Allah’s command.
3. The learner should make dua to Allah for rain and thank Him when it comes.

Answer: Allah sends provision, and Mikail carries out the duty of rain by His command. We ask Allah, not the angel.

## Activity: Match Jibril and Mikail with their duties
You will need: Flash cards of names and duties, Notebook

1. Place the name cards Jibril and Mikail on the desk.

2. Match them with the duty cards: revelation, and rain and provision.

3. In pairs, explain why each duty matters to a Grade 4 learner.

4. Write two sentences in your notebook, one for each angel.

studyPages.title: Lesson 3: Raqib, Atid, Izrail and Israfil
studyPages.body:
## Practice

1. What is the duty of Jibril?

2. What is the duty of Mikail?

3. Should a Muslim worship Jibril because he brought the Qur’an?

## Answers to practice

1. He brings Allah’s revelation to the prophets. He brought the Qur’an to Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.).

2. He is entrusted with rain and provision by Allah’s command.

3. No. Worship is for Allah alone. Jibril obeys Allah.

## Summary
• Jibril brought revelation, including the Qur’an, to the Prophet (S.A.W.).
• Mikail is entrusted with rain and provision.
• We thank Allah for both duties and we do not worship the angels.

LESSON 3: RAQIB, ATID, IZRAIL AND ISRAFIL
=========================================

## What you will learn
• Explain the duties of Raqib and Atid.
• Explain the duties of Malakul Maut and Israfil.
• Match each selected angel with the correct duty.

Curriculum outcomes: a) mention the names of the selected angels to strengthen their faith; b) explain the duties of the selected angels as a pillar of Iman

## Introduction
Two angels write what you say and do. Another will take the soul when the appointed time comes. Another will blow the trumpet that begins the Day of Judgement. Their names are part of a Muslim’s faith.

studyPages.title: Lesson 3: Raqib, Atid, Izrail and Israfil — Raqib and Atid
studyPages.body:
## Notes

### Raqib and Atid
Raqib and Atid are the recording angels who stay with every person. The Qur’an speaks of two receivers, one on the right and one on the left, and says that a person does not utter a word without an observer ready (Qur’an 50:17-18). It also speaks of noble scribes who record what people do (Qur’an 82:10-12). One records good deeds and the other records bad deeds. Nothing of that record is lost.

### Malakul Maut (Izrail)
Malakul Maut means the Angel of Death. The Qur’an says the angel of death will take the souls (Qur’an 32:11). He is also called Izrail in Islamic teaching. He takes a soul only when Allah has appointed that time. He does not act by his own wish. Remembering him should push a learner to obey Allah, not to tell frightening stories or to be cruel.

studyPages.title: Lesson 3: Raqib, Atid, Izrail and Israfil — Israfil
studyPages.body:
### Israfil
Israfil will blow the trumpet. The Qur’an describes a blast after which those in the heavens and the earth fall unconscious, except whom Allah wills, and a later blast after which they stand, looking (Qur’an 39:68). The first blast brings the end of this world as we know it, and the next blast is the resurrection for judgement.

Learn the four duties until you can match them without the chart: recorders, Angel of Death, and the angel of the trumpet. These duties are signs that this life is written, that it will end, and that it will be judged.

studyPages.title: Lesson 3: Raqib, Atid, Izrail and Israfil — Example 1
studyPages.body:
## Key words
• Raqib and Atid — the two angels who record a person’s deeds
• Malakul Maut (Izrail) — the Angel of Death, who takes souls by Allah’s command
• Israfil — the angel who will blow the trumpet

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Sort these duties under the right names: blowing the trumpet, taking the soul, writing good and bad deeds.

Working:
1. Israfil blows the trumpet.
2. Malakul Maut (Izrail) takes the soul at the appointed time.
3. Raqib and Atid record the deeds.

Answer: Israfil: the trumpet. Izrail: the soul. Raqib and Atid: the record of deeds.

studyPages.title: Lesson 3: Raqib, Atid, Izrail and Israfil — Angel crossword and matching cards
studyPages.body:
## Activity: Angel crossword and matching cards
You will need: A simple crossword or word search with the six names, Duty flash cards, Notebook

1. In pairs, find the names Jibril, Mikail, Raqib, Atid, Izrail and Israfil in the puzzle.

2. Match each name card with its duty card on the pocket board or desk.

3. Check another pair and correct any mismatch.

4. Write the full list of names and duties in your notebook.

## Practice

1. What do Raqib and Atid do?

2. Who is Malakul Maut, and what is his duty?

3. What will Israfil do?

4. Which Qur’an reference speaks of the two receivers who record words?

## Answers to practice

1. They record a person’s deeds. One records good deeds and the other records bad deeds.

2. He is the Angel of Death, also called Izrail. He takes souls when Allah has appointed the time.

3. He will blow the trumpet for the events of the Last Day, as the Qur’an describes.

4. Qur’an 50:17-18.

## Summary
• Raqib and Atid record good and bad deeds.
• Izrail, the Angel of Death, takes souls by Allah’s command.
• Israfil will blow the trumpet.

studyPages.title: Lesson 4: Living with belief in the angels
studyPages.body:
LESSON 4: LIVING WITH BELIEF IN THE ANGELS
==========================================

## What you will learn
• Explain how the duties of the angels affect daily choices.
• Show appreciation for the angels as Allah’s creation.
• Use a class qasida to remember names and duties.

Curriculum outcomes: b) explain the duties of the selected angels as a pillar of Iman; c) appreciate angels as Allah’s creation as a Pillar of Iman

## Introduction
Belief in the recording angels should make a person careful, not hopeless. A good word is written, and a bad word is written. This lesson turns that knowledge into careful speech and hopeful deeds.

## Notes

### Why Allah created the angels
Allah created the angels to worship Him and to carry out His commands. Their duties serve His wisdom: revelation is delivered, provision is managed by His leave, deeds are recorded, souls are taken at the right time, and the trumpet will be blown when He wills. They are a sign of His power and of His care for the universe.

studyPages.title: Lesson 4: Living with belief in the angels — What their duties mean for a learner
studyPages.body:
### What their duties mean for a learner
- Because Jibril brought the Qur’an, we recite it respectfully and follow it.
- Because Mikail’s duty concerns rain and rizq, we thank Allah for food and we do not waste it.
- Because Raqib and Atid write our deeds, we choose words and actions we would be happy to see in the record. A kind word is worth saying. A lie is not worth the line it will fill.
- Because Izrail will take the soul at an appointed time, we do not delay a good deed as if we owned tomorrow.
- Because Israfil will blow the trumpet, we believe the Day of Judgement is real and we prepare for it.

studyPages.title: Lesson 4: Living with belief in the angels — Example 1
studyPages.body:
### Appreciation
We appreciate the angels by believing in them, speaking of them with respect, and refusing jokes that insult them. We do not draw them as we imagine, and we do not worship them. A class qasida can help memory: “Jibril brought the Book we read, Mikail brings the rain we need, Raqib and Atid write the deed, Izrail calls the soul, Israfil’s trumpet wakes the world, by Allah’s leave alone.” Use the song to remember, and use your behaviour to show that the belief is alive.

## Key words
• record of deeds — the writing of good and bad actions kept by the recording angels
• appreciate — to value the angels by believing in them and respecting them

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Two learners start to mock a classmate with a rude nickname. One of them remembers Raqib and Atid. What changes?

Working:
1. The words would be recorded.
2. He stops the nickname and says a kind word instead.
3. The kind word is also recorded.

Answer: He stops the insult because it would be written, and he chooses a good word that will be written instead.

studyPages.title: Lesson 4: Living with belief in the angels — Qasida and a notebook of duties
studyPages.body:
## Activity: Qasida and a notebook of duties
You will need: Digital device to find a suitable qasida with the teacher, or the class lines above, Notebook

1. With the teacher, listen to or sing a qasida on the angels and their duties. If no suitable recording is available, learn the class lines.

2. In pairs, brainstorm how each duty touches your life and write five points.

3. Share one point with the class and listen respectfully to other opinions.

4. Copy the corrected points into your notebook.

studyPages.title: Lesson 4: Living with belief in the angels — Answers to practice
studyPages.body:
## Practice

1. Why did Allah create the angels?

2. How should belief in Raqib and Atid change a learner’s speech?

3. Give two ways of appreciating the angels without worshipping them.

## Answers to practice

1. To worship Him and to carry out His commands.

2. The learner avoids lies and insults because they are recorded, and chooses good words that are also recorded.

3. Believe in them, speak of them with respect, follow the Qur’an Jibril brought, and thank Allah for the duties they carry out.

## Summary
• Angels worship Allah and carry out His commands.
• Their duties encourage careful speech, thankfulness, and preparation for the Last Day.
• We respect angels and we worship Allah alone.

studyPages.title: Revision quiz
studyPages.body:
REVISION QUIZ
=============

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. Belief in the angels is…
   A. a story we may ignore
   B. a pillar of Iman
   C. a type of najasa
   D. only for adults

2. The angels were created from…
   A. clay
   B. light
   C. fire like the jinn only
   D. water

3. Who brought the Qur’an to Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.)?
   A. Mikail
   B. Israfil
   C. Jibril
   D. Raqib

4. Mikail is entrusted with…
   A. recording nicknames only
   B. rain and provision
   C. the trumpet only
   D. building the Ka’bah

5. Raqib and Atid are…
   A. the recording angels
   B. two prophets
   C. two surahs
   D. types of wudhu

6. Malakul Maut (Izrail) takes the soul…

7. Who will blow the trumpet?
   A. Jibril
   B. Mikail
   C. Israfil
   D. Atid

8. Which verse group speaks of two angels receiving a person’s words?
   A. Qur’an 50:17-18
   B. Qur’an 1:1 only
   C. A class song only
   D. Qur’an 112 only

9. A learner stops an insult because it will be written. This shows belief in which angels?
   A. Raqib and Atid
   B. only the rules of football
   C. Al-Masad as an angel
   D. horse riding

10. What is the correct way to appreciate the angels?
   A. worship them
   B. believe in them, respect them, and worship Allah alone
   C. deny them until we see them
   D. draw them as we imagine

studyPages.title: Quiz answers
studyPages.body:
ANSWERS
=======

1. B. a pillar of Iman
   It is one of the pillars of faith.

2. B. light
   Sahih Muslim reports that the angels were created from light.

3. C. Jibril
   Jibril is the angel of revelation.

4. B. rain and provision
   His duty concerns rain and rizq, by Allah’s command.

5. A. the recording angels
   They record good and bad deeds.

6. When Allah has appointed that person’s time.
   He acts by Allah’s command, as the Angel of Death.

7. C. Israfil
   Israfil will blow the trumpet for the events described in the Qur’an.

8. A. Qur’an 50:17-18
   Surat Qaf describes the two receivers, on the right and on the left.

9. A. Raqib and Atid
   The recording angels write what people say and do.

10. B. believe in them, respect them, and worship Allah alone
   They are honoured creation. Worship belongs to Allah alone.
